Belarusian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *razъ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ras]

Adverb

[edit]

раз • (raz)

  1. once

Noun

[edit]

раз • (raz) m inan (genitive ра́зу, nominative plural разы́, genitive plural разо́ў)

  1. time (an instance or occurrence)

Eastern Mari

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Probably from Russian раз (raz).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ɾɑz/
  • Rhymes: -ɑz
  • Hyphenation: раз

Conjunction

[edit]

раз • (raz)

  1. if, since
    раз йодат, ыштем
    raz jodat, yštem
    if you ask me, I'll do it

References

[edit]
  • J. Bradley et al. (2023), “раз”, in The Mari Web Project: Mari-English Dictionary, University of Vienna

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]
Pannonian Rusyn numbers (edit)
1 2  → [a], [b], [c]
    Cardinal: єден (jeden)
    Ordinal: перши (perši)
    Adverbial: раз (raz), воєдно (vojedno), оєдно (ojedno)
    Multiplier: єднїсти (jednjisti)
    Collective: єдни (jedni)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak raz, from Proto-Slavic *razъ. Cognates include Carpathian Rusyn раз (raz) and Slovak raz.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈras]
  • Rhymes: -as
  • Hyphenation: раз

Adverb

[edit]

раз (raz) (not comparable)

  1. once, one time
    йому досц раз повесц ― jomu dosc raz povesc ― it's enough to tell him once
    раз (за) навше ― raz (za) navše ― once and for all
  2. once, formerly, once upon a time [with дакеди (dakedi) or давно (davno)]
    Synonym: дакеди (dakedi)
    бул раз єден краль ― bul raz jeden kralʹ ― there was once a king
  3. suddenly, at once
    Synonym: нараз (naraz)
    раз лєм загирми ― raz ljem zahirmi ― suddenly it just thunders
  4. time, times (instance or occurrence; ratio of comparison)
    остатнї раз ― ostatnji raz ― last time
    два раз векши ― dva raz vekši ― two times bigger
    кельо раз сом ци гуторел!
    kelʹo raz som ci hutorel!
    how many times have I told you!
  5. (arithmetic) times (multiplied by)
    штири раз штири шеснац ― štiri raz štiri šesnac ― four times four is sixteen

Usage notes

[edit]
  • For Sense 4, unlike in Polish and East Slavic, the term is not declined following numbers, possibly due to influence from Serbo-Croatian пут / put.

Conjunction

[edit]

раз (raz)

  1. (usually repeated) now, sometimes (suggesting contrasting possibilities each as likely to happen or happening as frequently as the others; suggesting that someone or something behaves erratically)
    роби раз єдно раз друге
    robi raz jedno raz druhe
    now he does one thing, now he does another
    видумує раз тото раз гевто
    vidumuje raz toto raz hevto
    now he wants this, now that
    раз єден раз два ― raz jeden raz dva ― alternately, in turns (literally, “now one now two”)

Noun

[edit]

раз (raz) m inan

  1. moment, opportunity, occasion
    Synonym: завод (zavod)
    од першого разу ― od peršoho razu ― immediately (literally, “from the first opportunity”)

Russian

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • разъ (raz) — pre-1918 spelling

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic разъ (razŭ, “strike”), from Proto-Slavic *razъ. Cognate to рази́ть (razítʹ), ре́зать (rézatʹ). For the semantic shift, compare Polish raz.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ras]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Homophone: рас (ras)
  • Rhymes: -as

Noun

[edit]

раз • (raz) m inan (genitive ра́за, nominative plural разы́, genitive plural раз, relational adjective ра́зовый, diminutive разо́к or ра́зик)

  1. time (an instance or occurrence)
    два ра́за ― dva ráza ― twice
    ещё раз ― ješčó raz ― once more; one more time
    ни ра́зу ― ni rázu ― not once; never
    не раз ― ne raz ― repeatedly
    как раз ― kak raz ― just; just in time
    за раз ― za raz ― at a time
  2. one (in counting)
    раз, два, три ... марш! ― raz, dva, tri ... marš! ― one, two, three ... go!
    раз, два, три, ого́нь! ― raz, dva, tri, ogónʹ! ― one, two, three, fire!

Adverb

[edit]

раз • (raz)

  1. (colloquial) once, one day, once upon a time
    Synonyms: одна́жды (odnáždy), ка́к-то (kák-to), ка́к-то раз (kák-to raz), не́когда (nékogda)
    Я ви́дел раз её в весёлом ви́хре ба́ла…
    Ja vídel raz jejó v vesjólom víxre bála…
    I saw her once in the merry whirlwind of a ball… (M. Yu. Lermontov, Verse #145)

Conjunction

[edit]

раз • (raz)

  1. (colloquial) if, since; as long as
    Synonyms: е́сли (jésli), ко́ли (kóli), коль (kolʹ)
    Сади́сь, раз пришёл. ― Sadísʹ, raz prišól. ― Sit down, as long as you’ve come.
    Раз он так сказа́л, зна́чит, так и бу́дет! ― Raz on tak skazál, znáčit, tak i búdet! ― Since he said so, this is how it’s going to be!

Derived terms

[edit]
  • раз та́к (raz ták, “in that case”)

[edit]
  • >? Eastern Mari: раз (raz)

Ukrainian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *razъ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [raz]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

раз • (raz) m inan (genitive ра́зу or (See usage notes) ра́за, nominative plural рази́, genitive plural разі́в or раз)

  1. time (instance or occurrence)
    цього́ ра́зу (adverbial) ― cʹohó rázu ― this time
    насту́пного ра́зу (adverbial) ― nastúpnoho rázu ― next time
    мину́лого ра́зу (adverbial) ― mynúloho rázu ― last time
    раз на ти́ждень (adverbial) ― raz na týždenʹ ― once a week
  2. a case occurring (clarification of this definition is needed)
  3. time (ratio of comparison)
    у чоти́ри з полови́ною рази́ бі́льше ― u čotýry z polovýnoju razý bílʹše ― four-and-a-half times more
    у ві́сім разі́в бі́льший ― u vísim razív bílʹšyj ― eight times bigger
  4. one (when counting things, or counting off)
    Synonym: оди́н (odýn)
    раз, два, три, чоти́ри... ― raz, dva, try, čotýry... ― one, two, three, four...

Usage notes

[edit]

In the 'ratio of comparison' sense, some sources stipulate that a variant genitive form раза should be used after a number containing a decimal point (comma) or after півтора́ (“one-and-a-half”), for instance: у 2,3 раза ― 2.3 times.[1][2]

[edit]

раз • (raz)

  1. once, one day, once upon a time
    Synonyms: коли́сь (kolýsʹ), один раз (odyn raz), одного разу (odnoho razu)
    раз я пішов на річку… ― raz ja pišov na ričku… ― one day I went to the river…

[edit]

раз • (raz)

  1. (colloquial) if; since; as long as
